title: Digital ID Proclamation 1284/2023: registrant owns personal data; authentication requires consent
claim: The Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023 provides that the registrant owns any personal data collected for the Digital Identification System and that authentication processes shall be done with the consent of the registrant.
evidence_summary: Article 17(1) of Proclamation No. 1284/2023 states that the owner of personal data collected for the Digital Identification System is the Registrant, and any authentication processes shall be done with the consent of the Registrant. Article 17(4) prohibits collection, distribution, use or disclosure of such data without the Registrant's consent.
source_excerpt: 17. Protection and Security of Personal Data 1/ The owner of any Personal Data collected for the Digital Identification System is the Registrant; Hence any authentication processes under the Digital Identification System shall be done with the consent of the Registrant... 4/ Any person may not collect, distribute, print, use, provide data or transfer a copy to a third party or body or disclose data collected with Digital Identification System without the Registrant's consent.
interpretation: Normative evidence that Ethiopia's foundational digital ID law establishes a consent-based data governance architecture with the registrant as data owner. This is what the law requires; it does not evidence consent practice in the field.
citation: Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023, Art. 17(1), 17(4) (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 19, 18 April 2023).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 17).
keywords: digital ID, Fayda, consent, personal data, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/2/eth_digital_id_1284.pdf); locator Article 17, pages 18-20.

title: Digital ID Proclamation 1284/2023: standard consent form at registration
claim: The Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023 requires registrants to complete and sign a standard consent form describing their rights and obligations as proof of consent at registration.
evidence_summary: Article 17(10) requires that during registration a standard consent form prepared by the Digital Identification System describing the Registrant's rights and obligations be completed and signed by the Registrant as proof of consent.
source_excerpt: 10/ During registration, a standard consent form prepared by Digital Identification System, which describe the Registrant's rights and obligations shall be completed and signed by the Registrant as proof of consent.
interpretation: Normative evidence of a documentary consent mechanism in the digital ID registration process. Establishes the required procedure; does not evidence whether the form is understood or freely given in practice.
citation: Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023, Art. 17(10) (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 19, 18 April 2023).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 17(10)).
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/2/eth_digital_id_1284.pdf); locator Article 17(10).

title: Digital ID Proclamation 1284/2023: grievance and complaint redressal
claim: The Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023 requires the Digital ID Institution to establish a complaint handling department and provides that persons may lodge complaints and, if dissatisfied, file a complaint to the court.
evidence_summary: Article 20 ('Grievance and Complaint Redressal') requires the Institution to establish a complaint handling department and notify customers; any person against whom Digital Identification service is provided has the right to lodge a complaint; grievances are handled per the Institution's grievance directive; dissatisfied parties may file a complaint to the pertinent court.
source_excerpt: 20. Grievance and Complaint Redressal 1/ The Institution shall establish a complaint handling department and notify such establishments to its customers. 2/ Any person against whom Digital Identification service is provided and a decision is made has the right to lodge a complaint to the Institution... 3/ Any complaints and grievances... shall be solved in accordance with the grievance filing and redressal Directive of the Institution. 4/ A party who is dissatisfied with the decisions of the Institution may file a complaint to the pertinent court.
interpretation: Normative/institutional evidence of a mandated grievance mechanism and court recourse for digital ID decisions. Establishes formal accountability structures; does not evidence their operational effectiveness.
citation: Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023, Art. 20 (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 19, 18 April 2023).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 20).
keywords: grievance, complaint, redress, accountability, digital ID, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/2/eth_digital_id_1284.pdf); locator Article 20.

title: Digital ID Proclamation 1284/2023: relying parties require approval and consent-based data access
claim: The Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023 requires relying parties to obtain approval from the concerned regulator before making Digital Identification mandatory, and requires registrant consent before receiving personal data for authentication.
evidence_summary: Article 15 provides that a relying party wanting to make Digital Identification mandatory for a service must get approval from the concerned regulator, and relying parties may receive a Registrant's personal data to authenticate identity based on the consent of the Registrant.
source_excerpt: 15. Relying Parties 1/Any Relying Party that wants to put Digital Identification as a mandatory requirement to provide service shall get approval from the concerned regulator. 2/ Relying Parties may receive a Registrant's Personal Data from the Institution or other Authentication Service Providers authorized by the Institution, to authenticate the individual's identity based on the consent of the Registrant.
interpretation: Normative evidence of controls on the use of digital ID as a service gatekeeper: mandatory-use requires regulatory approval and data access is consent-based. Establishes formal safeguards; does not evidence real-world gatekeeping.
citation: Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023, Art. 15(1)-(2) (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 19, 18 April 2023).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 15).
keywords: relying parties, authentication, consent, digital ID, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/2/eth_digital_id_1284.pdf); locator Article 15.
